key_insight: An EHR-integrated generative AI tool improved venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk detection sensitivity compared with checklist-based and clinician-selected order sets, while sacrificing some specificity.
clinical_relevance: For inpatient thromboprophylaxis workflows, this suggests AI may help catch more high-risk patients, but it should augment—not replace—clinician judgment.
method: Multisite retrospective validation at Johns Hopkins Medicine inpatient sites
Compared iHGR and clinician order-set classifications against physician-adjudicated chart review reference standard
Balanced random sample of 500 admissions drawn from 758 eligible cases across two order-set periods
evidence_signal: In this real-world evaluation, iHGR reached 81.8% sensitivity and 70.9% specificity, outperforming the checklist order set on sensitivity and the clinician-judgment order set on sensitivity while remaining within a trade-off range on specificity.
watch_item: False negatives were linked to missed narrative risk factors, highlighting the need to improve extraction from free-text clinical data before broader deployment.
paper_title: Multisite Real-World Validation of an Electronic Health Record-Integrated Generative Artificial Intelligence Tool for Venous Thromboembolism Risk Stratification
